requirements.name: SystemArchitecture
requirements.description: The Chemical Detector system is an autonomous mobile robot that searches for the source of a target chemical in an unknown environment. It carries a Vehicle with gas sensors, an obstacle detector, and an odometer, and is capable of moving with configurable linear velocity and turning to any of four directions (Left, Right, Back, Front) relative to its body. The system operates in a continuous sense-analyse-act loop until the chemical source is confirmed.

requirements.name: ControllerArchitecture
requirements.description: The Chemical Detector is composed of three subsystems: (1) a sensing-and-actuation surface — the Vehicle — that exposes sensor events (gas, obstacle, odometer) and provides movement operations (move, randomWalk, shortRandomWalk); (2) a gas-analysis subsystem that classifies sensor readings and decides whether to keep searching, change direction towards a stronger signal, or stop because the chemical source has been found; and (3) a movement subsystem that performs random-walk search, follows direction commands, handles obstacle avoidance, and recovers when stuck. The two reasoning subsystems communicate only via the turn, stop, and resume events; the movement subsystem emits the flag event to the Vehicle when the chemical source is found.

requirements.name: StatusEnum
requirements.description: The Status enumeration captures the outcome of a single gas-analysis cycle. It has exactly two values: noGas (current reading does not indicate the target chemical) and gasD (current reading indicates the target chemical is present).

requirements.name: AngleEnum
requirements.description: The Angle enumeration represents a turn direction relative to the robot body. It has exactly four values: Left, Right, Back, Front. The movement subsystem uses Angle values as the operand of the move operation.

requirements.name: LocEnum
requirements.description: The Loc enumeration represents the side of the robot on which an obstacle has been detected. It has exactly three values: left, right, front. The movement subsystem receives Loc values through the obstacle event and passes them to the changeDirection operation.

requirements.name: ChemType
requirements.description: Chem is an opaque type representing the identity of a chemical species. Sensor readings carry a Chem value to identify which chemical the reading is for. Equality is the only operation needed on Chem.

requirements.name: IntensityType
requirements.description: Intensity is a totally-ordered type representing the strength of a sensor reading. The system compares two intensities via the goreq function (see CD-Fn4). Comparison is the only operation needed on Intensity.

requirements.name: GasSensorRecord
requirements.description: A GasSensor is a record with two fields: c (Chem, the chemical identity) and i (Intensity, the measured intensity for that chemical). The Vehicle's gas event carries a sequence of GasSensor values (Seq(GasSensor)) representing a multi-sensor reading at one point in time.

requirements.name: GasSensorReading
requirements.description: A GasSensorReading is a sequence of GasSensor values produced by the Vehicle's gas event. The position in the sequence (1-based index) encodes which sensor produced the reading, and is mapped to a direction by the angle function. The gas-analysis subsystem stores the most recent reading in the gs state variable.

requirements.name: IntensityThreshold
requirements.description: The constant thr (Intensity) is the intensity threshold for declaring a chemical source 'found'. When the peak intensity of the current gas reading is at or above thr, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions to its final state and the movement subsystem emits the flag event. The value is configured at system startup and does not change at run time.

requirements.name: LinearVelocity
requirements.description: The constant lv (real) is the linear velocity (in arbitrary units) at which the Vehicle moves during normal travel. It is the first argument to every move(lv, a) call made by the movement subsystem. The value is configured at system startup.

requirements.name: EvadeTime
requirements.description: The constant evadeTime (nat) is the duration the system waits inside the Avoiding state after issuing a changeDirection command. This gives the changeDirection action time to complete before the next behaviour fires.

requirements.name: StuckPeriod
requirements.description: The constant stuckPeriod (nat) is the time-window threshold for the stuck-detection rule. If less time than stuckPeriod has elapsed since the first obstacle of the current evasion sequence, the robot is considered to be making progress and continues avoiding; otherwise the recovery behaviour activates.

requirements.name: StuckDist
requirements.description: The constant stuckDist (real) is the distance threshold for stuck detection. If the robot has travelled more than stuckDist between the first and second obstacles of an evasion sequence (d1 - d0 > stuckDist), it is considered to have escaped; otherwise it is considered stuck and the recovery behaviour activates.

requirements.name: OutPeriod
requirements.description: The constant outPeriod (nat) is the duration the robot spends in the GettingOut state executing a shortRandomWalk after stuck detection has fired. It bounds the recovery manoeuvre before the robot returns to normal navigation.

requirements.name: AnalysisFunction
requirements.description: The analysis function takes a sequence of GasSensor readings and returns a Status: noGas if no reading indicates the target chemical, gasD otherwise. This is the primary classifier used by the gas-analysis subsystem to decide whether the Vehicle should keep moving or stop.

requirements.name: IntensityFunction
requirements.description: The intensity function takes a non-empty sequence of GasSensor readings and returns the maximum intensity across the sequence. Precondition: the input sequence is non-empty. Postcondition: the result is greater than or equal to every i field in the input, and the result equals some sensor's i field.

requirements.name: LocationFunction
requirements.description: The location function takes a non-empty sequence of GasSensor readings and returns the Angle of the sensor with the highest intensity. Precondition: the input sequence is non-empty. Postcondition: there exists an index x such that gs[x].i equals intensity(gs) and the result equals angle(x). Used to steer the robot towards the strongest signal.

requirements.name: IntensityCompare
requirements.description: The goreq function (intensity-greater-or-equal) compares two Intensity values and returns true iff the first is at least as large as the second. It is the only ordering predicate needed on Intensity and is used in the threshold check (intensity(gs) >= thr) and inside the intensity function's correctness condition.

requirements.name: GasEvent
requirements.description: The gas event carries a value of type Seq(GasSensor) representing one multi-sensor gas reading. The Vehicle emits gas; the gas-analysis subsystem receives it and stores the sequence in the gs variable for the gas-analysis subsystem to process.

requirements.name: ObstacleEvent
requirements.description: The obstacle event carries a value of type Loc indicating the side of the robot on which an obstacle has been detected. The Vehicle emits obstacle; the movement subsystem receives it and stores the value in the l variable for the movement subsystem.

requirements.name: OdometerEvent
requirements.description: The odometer event carries a value of type real representing the current cumulative distance travelled by the Vehicle. The Vehicle emits odometer; the movement subsystem consumes the value into the d0 or d1 variable to support stuck detection.

requirements.name: TurnEvent
requirements.description: The turn event carries a value of type Angle indicating the direction the robot should face next. The gas-analysis subsystem emits turn (with the result of the location function); the movement subsystem consumes it to update the a variable and trigger movement transitions.

requirements.name: StopEvent
requirements.description: The stop signal event (no payload) is emitted by the gas-analysis subsystem when the chemical source has been confirmed (peak intensity is at or above thr). The movement subsystem consumes stop to transition the movement subsystem to the Found state.

requirements.name: ResumeEvent
requirements.description: The resume signal event (no payload) is emitted by the gas-analysis subsystem after analysing a no-gas reading. The movement subsystem consumes resume to return its movement subsystem to the Waiting state and continue searching.

requirements.name: FlagEvent
requirements.description: The flag signal event (no payload) is emitted by the movement subsystem upon entering the Found state. It signals to the Vehicle that the chemical source has been located so the platform may halt and report.

requirements.name: OperationMove
requirements.description: The move(lv : real, a : Angle) operation is provided by the Vehicle. Calling move causes the Vehicle to move with linear velocity lv in direction a (relative to the robot body). The operation does not terminate on its own; subsequent move calls override the previous one. Calling move(0, Angle::Front) halts the Vehicle.

requirements.name: OperationRandomWalk
requirements.description: The randomWalk() operation is provided by the Vehicle. It performs an unbounded random-walk search. The robot invokes randomWalk while in the Waiting state to keep moving between sensor readings.

requirements.name: OperationShortRandomWalk
requirements.description: The shortRandomWalk() operation is provided by the Vehicle and runs for a bounded period of time. The robot invokes shortRandomWalk on entry to the GettingOut state to perform a recovery manoeuvre when stuck detection has fired.

requirements.name: OperationChangeDirection
requirements.description: The changeDirection(l : Loc) operation is invoked from the Avoiding-state entry behaviour. Its specified behaviour is: if l == Loc::left then move(lv, Angle::Right); if l == Loc::right then move(lv, Angle::Left); if l == Loc::front then move(lv, Angle::Back). lv is provided to the operation as a real constant.

requirements.name: Variable_gs
requirements.description: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable gs of type Seq(GasSensor) initialised to the empty sequence. gs is overwritten on every gas-event reception (Reading -> Analysis transition) and read by the analysis, intensity, and location functions.

requirements.name: Variable_sts
requirements.description: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable sts of type Status. sts is assigned in the Analysis state entry action (sts = analysis(gs)) and used as a guard in the transitions leaving Analysis.

requirements.name: Variable_ins
requirements.description: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable ins of type Intensity. ins is assigned in the GasDetected state entry action (ins = intensity(gs)) and compared against thr in the transitions leaving GasDetected.

requirements.name: Variable_anl
requirements.description: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable anl of type Angle. anl is assigned during the GasDetected -> Reading transition (anl = location(gs)) and immediately sent over the turn event in the same transition action.

requirements.name: Variable_a
requirements.description: The movement subsystem maintains a state variable a of type Angle. a is overwritten every time the turn event is received (turn ? a) and read by the Going / TryingAgain entry actions to call move(lv, a).

requirements.name: Variable_d0
requirements.description: The movement subsystem maintains a state variable d0 of type real. d0 is assigned in the Avoiding state entry action (odometer ? d0) and used by stuck detection (d1 - d0 > stuckDist) to decide whether the robot is making progress.

requirements.name: Variable_d1
requirements.description: The movement subsystem maintains a state variable d1 of type real. d1 is assigned in the TryingAgain -> AvoidingAgain transition action (odometer ? d1) and used together with d0 by stuck detection.

requirements.name: Variable_l
requirements.description: The movement subsystem maintains a state variable l of type Loc. l is assigned on every obstacle event reception (obstacle ? l) and passed to changeDirection(l) in the Avoiding state entry action.

requirements.name: Clock_T
requirements.description: The movement subsystem maintains a clock T used by stuck-detection. T is reset on the Going -> Avoiding transition and on the AvoidingAgain -> Avoiding transition. The predicate since(T) returns the elapsed time since the last reset and is compared against stuckPeriod in the behaviours leaving AvoidingAgain.

requirements.name: GA_StateNoGas
requirements.description: NoGas is a state of the gas-analysis subsystem reached after analysis classifies a reading as not indicating the target chemical. NoGas has no entry, during, or exit actions. The only transition out of NoGas returns to Reading; the resume event is sent on the way in.

requirements.name: GA_StateReading
requirements.description: Reading is the initial state of the gas-analysis subsystem: control transitions from the initial state to Reading on system start. Reading has no entry, during, or exit actions. The only transition out of Reading consumes a gas event and moves to Analysis.

requirements.name: GA_StateAnalysis
requirements.description: Analysis is the state where the gas-analysis subsystem classifies the most recent reading. On entry, the analysis function is applied to gs and the result is assigned to sts. Analysis has two outgoing transitions, both guarded by sts and both leaving Analysis on the same step.

requirements.name: GA_StateGasDetected
requirements.description: GasDetected is the state entered when analysis returned gasD. On entry, the intensity function is applied to gs and the result is assigned to ins. GasDetected has two outgoing transitions guarded by the comparison goreq(ins, thr): one to the final state j1 (above threshold; send stop), one back to Reading (below threshold; turn towards the strongest signal and continue).

requirements.name: MV_StateWaiting
requirements.description: Waiting is the initial state of the movement subsystem. The during action is randomWalk(), so while no event is being processed the robot performs unbounded random-walk search. Waiting receives turn (-> Going), stop (-> Found), and resume (-> Waiting self-loop) events.

requirements.name: MV_StateGoing
requirements.description: Going is the state where the robot moves with linear velocity lv in direction a. The entry action move(lv, a) starts the motion. Going self-loops on a new turn event (re-issues move with the new angle), transitions to Found on stop, to Avoiding on obstacle, and to Waiting on resume.

requirements.name: MV_StateFound
requirements.description: Found is the state entered when the chemical source has been confirmed. The entry action sends the flag event to the Vehicle and immediately calls move(0, Angle::Front) to halt the platform. The only transition out of Found goes to the final state j1.

requirements.name: MV_StateAvoiding
requirements.description: Avoiding is the state entered when an obstacle has been detected during normal travel. The entry action sequences three operations: odometer ? d0 (record current distance), changeDirection(l) (turn away from the obstacle), wait(evadeTime) (give the turn time to complete). Avoiding transitions to TryingAgain on turn, to Found on stop, and to Waiting on resume.

requirements.name: MV_StateTryingAgain
requirements.description: TryingAgain is the state where the robot resumes movement after an avoidance manoeuvre. The entry action move(lv, a) restarts motion in the most recent direction a. TryingAgain self-loops on a new turn event, transitions to Found on stop, to Waiting on resume, and to AvoidingAgain on a fresh obstacle (with action odometer ? d1 to seed stuck detection).

requirements.name: MV_StateAvoidingAgain
requirements.description: AvoidingAgain is the state entered after a second obstacle is hit during a single evasion sequence. It has no entry, during, or exit actions. AvoidingAgain has two guarded transitions: back to Avoiding when the robot is judged to be making progress (since(T) < stuckPeriod OR d1 - d0 > stuckDist), or to GettingOut when stuck (since(T) >= stuckPeriod AND d1 - d0 <= stuckDist). It also transitions to Found on stop and to Waiting on resume.

requirements.name: MV_StateGettingOut
requirements.description: GettingOut is the recovery state entered when stuck detection has fired. The entry action sequences shortRandomWalk() (a terminating random-walk) and wait(outPeriod) (bounded wait). GettingOut transitions to Going on turn, to Found on stop, and to Waiting on resume.

requirements.name: GA_Init
requirements.description: On system startup, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions from its initial state to Reading. No guard, no trigger, no action.

requirements.name: GA_Reading_to_Analysis
requirements.description: In Reading, on receiving the gas event with payload gs, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions to Analysis. Trigger: gas ? gs. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: GA_NoGas_to_Reading
requirements.description: In NoGas, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions back to Reading. No guard, no trigger, no action. This is an autonomous transition that allows the next reading to be collected.

requirements.name: GA_Analysis_to_NoGas
requirements.description: In Analysis, when the entry-action result sts equals Status::noGas, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions to NoGas. Guard: sts == Status::noGas. Action: send resume (so the movement subsystem returns to Waiting and continues searching). No trigger.

requirements.name: GA_Analysis_to_GasDetected
requirements.description: In Analysis, when the entry-action result sts equals Status::gasD, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions to GasDetected. Guard: sts == Status::gasD. No trigger, no action.

requirements.name: GA_GasDetected_to_Final
requirements.description: In GasDetected, when the peak intensity ins is at or above thr, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions to its final state j1. Guard: goreq(ins, thr). Action: send stop (so the movement subsystem moves to Found and halts).

requirements.name: GA_GasDetected_to_Reading
requirements.description: In GasDetected, when the peak intensity ins is below thr, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions back to Reading. Guard: NOT goreq(ins, thr). Action: anl = location(gs); send turn ! anl (so the movement subsystem steers towards the strongest signal).

requirements.name: MV_Init
requirements.description: On system startup, the movement subsystem transitions from its initial state to Waiting. No guard, no trigger, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Waiting_to_Going
requirements.description: In Waiting, on receiving the turn event with payload a, the movement subsystem transitions to Going. Trigger: turn ? a. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Waiting_self_resume
requirements.description: In Waiting, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem self-loops back to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action. (Resume in Waiting is effectively a no-op but is permitted so cross-state resume transitions are uniformly handled.)

requirements.name: MV_Waiting_to_Found
requirements.description: In Waiting, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Going_self_turn
requirements.description: In Going, on receiving the turn event with payload a, the movement subsystem self-loops back to Going. Trigger: turn ? a. No guard, no action. Re-entering Going re-fires the entry action move(lv, a) with the new angle.

requirements.name: MV_Going_to_Found
requirements.description: In Going, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Going_to_Avoiding
requirements.description: In Going, on receiving the obstacle event with payload l, the movement subsystem transitions to Avoiding. Trigger: obstacle ? l. Action: reset clock T so stuck detection can measure the new evasion sequence. No guard.

requirements.name: MV_Going_to_Waiting
requirements.description: In Going, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem transitions to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Found_to_Final
requirements.description: In Found, the movement subsystem transitions to its final state j1. No guard, no trigger, no action. Found's entry action has already sent the flag event and halted the platform.

requirements.name: MV_Avoiding_to_TryingAgain
requirements.description: In Avoiding, on receiving the turn event with payload a, the movement subsystem transitions to TryingAgain. Trigger: turn ? a. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Avoiding_to_Found
requirements.description: In Avoiding, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_Avoiding_to_Waiting
requirements.description: In Avoiding, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem transitions to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_TryingAgain_self_turn
requirements.description: In TryingAgain, on receiving the turn event with payload a, the movement subsystem self-loops back to TryingAgain. Trigger: turn ? a. Re-entering TryingAgain re-fires move(lv, a) with the new angle.

requirements.name: MV_TryingAgain_to_Found
requirements.description: In TryingAgain, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_TryingAgain_to_Waiting
requirements.description: In TryingAgain, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem transitions to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_TryingAgain_to_AvoidingAgain
requirements.description: In TryingAgain, on receiving the obstacle event with payload l, the movement subsystem transitions to AvoidingAgain. Trigger: obstacle ? l. Action: odometer ? d1 (record current distance for stuck detection). No guard.

requirements.name: MV_AvoidingAgain_to_Avoiding
requirements.description: In AvoidingAgain, the movement subsystem transitions back to Avoiding when stuck detection judges the robot to be making progress: since(T) < stuckPeriod OR d1 - d0 > stuckDist. Action: reset clock T. No trigger.

requirements.name: MV_AvoidingAgain_to_GettingOut
requirements.description: In AvoidingAgain, the movement subsystem transitions to GettingOut when stuck detection fires: since(T) >= stuckPeriod AND d1 - d0 <= stuckDist. No trigger, no action.

requirements.name: MV_AvoidingAgain_to_Found
requirements.description: In AvoidingAgain, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_AvoidingAgain_to_Waiting
requirements.description: In AvoidingAgain, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem transitions to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_GettingOut_to_Going
requirements.description: In GettingOut, on receiving the turn event with payload a, the movement subsystem transitions to Going. Trigger: turn ? a. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_GettingOut_to_Found
requirements.description: In GettingOut, on receiving the stop event, the movement subsystem transitions to Found. Trigger: stop. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: MV_GettingOut_to_Waiting
requirements.description: In GettingOut, on receiving the resume event, the movement subsystem transitions to Waiting. Trigger: resume. No guard, no action.

requirements.name: UniqueTransitions
requirements.description: Each behavioural requirement (CD-GA-Beh1..7 and CD-MV-Beh1..23) maps to exactly one transition. There are no duplicate transitions for the same source state and trigger event combination. Implementations must not collapse or duplicate transitions.
